prompt: Build a single-page editorial site for a modern pinsa romana restaurant in Next.js with Tailwind v4. It should look exactly like our 1680x900 Figma frames on a 14-inch laptop and a 5K display alike: hero with a big sand arc and a cut-out pizza, a manifesto, a full-bleed video section showing the wood oven, a menu grid, some stats, a gallery and a footer.
expected_output: A Next 16 app whose desktop layout is on the fluid scale (fluid-* utilities, fluid-container once per section on its inner wrapper, the video sized in fluid units with its dimensions reserved against CLS), generated with `fluid init`/`fluid generate`, and passing `fluid check` + `fluid audit` + `fluid verify`.
assertions: the generated engine defines --fluid from the band's registered settings (min()/max() only, no clamp(), the ×1000 precision form)
sections use fluid utilities at lg (>= 40 occurrences)
the page container utility (fluid-container: max-width var(--fluid-container-width), padding-inline var(--fluid-container-padding)) is applied on each section's inner wrapper
audit.mjs reports zero errors
fluid check passes (generated output matches fluid.config.json, no bad settings)
verify-matrix passes

prompt: Same restaurant page but we're not a React shop: Vite, plain TypeScript and SCSS. Our frames are 1600 wide with 64px gutters and we don't want things to grow past 1.6x on huge monitors.
expected_output: A Vite build using generator-produced SCSS (`fluid.config.json` set to output.stack "scss"), with the non-default numbers — container width 1600, padding 64, growth ceiling 1.6 — set as `--fluid-desktop-container-width` / `-container-padding` / `-scale-max` in the project's own top-level `:root` (a SETTING, not a config key: no regenerate needed to tune them), passing `fluid check` + `fluid audit` + `fluid verify` including the ceiling viewport at 2560x1440.
assertions: the non-default numbers are settings in the project's own CSS, not fluid.config.json keys
SCSS layer generated by `fluid generate` (header comment present)
the desktop unit's max arm reads the scale-max setting (var(--_fluid-max)), not a baked-in literal
audit zero errors
fluid check passes on the scss/vite config
verify-matrix passes with non-default settings, ceiling viewport exercised

prompt: after I edited globals.css and restarted the dev server my scroll video on the homepage just sits on the first frame and then jumps to the end, and the video is full width with no gutters anymore. what broke in ScrubStage?
expected_output: Diagnoses a stale stylesheet (missing fluid-* rules, or a --fluid-build stamp that doesn't match what fluid.config.json generates now) before touching scrub code; gives the --fluid-build computed-style check and `fluid explain <W>x<H> --url <url> --brief` (verdict STALE; `fluid probe` is its old name), and the close-tab / rm -rf .next fix; explains why missing fluid-h removes the pin's travel.
assertions: identifies stale stylesheet, not a code bug
gives the --fluid-build computed-style check or fluid explain --url (--brief)
fix: close tab / fresh tab, then rm -rf .next
does not propose editing ScrubStage

prompt: Accessibility audit came back on our fluid marketing site: on a 27-inch monitor, Cmd+ zooming to 150% or 200% barely makes the text bigger. Our type is all lg:fluid-copy-* / lg:fluid-display-*. Is this our bug, and how do we fix it without breaking the layout?
expected_output: Explains that vw/svh-derived units cancel desktop zoom (CSS viewport shrinks by the zoom factor) and that text only grows once the viewport falls below the desktop band's minWidth; distinguishes zoom from the browser font-size setting; installs the generated zoom runtime first in <head> before first paint (`<FluidHead/>` for Next, `fluidPlugin()` for Vite, otherwise `runtime/zoom.classic.js` as the first classic <script>, or FLUID_ZOOM_INLINE pasted into it; a nonce or FLUID_ZOOM_SHA256 under a strict CSP) with `zoom: true` in fluid.config.json (type roles read --fluid-z, which folds in --fluid-zoom; --fluid itself, the layout unit, is never multiplied by zoom, so layout keeps fitting); verifies with `fluid verify`'s zoom row; mentions the mobile-handover step, and that Chromium and Safari are compensated while Firefox reads 1 (no reliable signal).
assertions: names the mechanism: zoom shrinks the CSS viewport, cancelling vw/svh units
does not propose a rem-anchored twin or adding a rem intercept to --fluid
installs the generated zoom runtime (FluidHead / fluidPlugin / zoom.classic.js / FLUID_ZOOM_INLINE, installFluidZoom) with zoom: true
compensates type only, not layout
verifies with the zoom row

prompt: We just added fluid-design v2 to our Next + shadcn/ui app (fluid init ran, src/styles/fluid exists). Our Button takes className and uses cn from src/lib/utils.ts. Passing className="lg:fluid-px-24" to a Button that already has lg:fluid-px-40 ships both classes. Fix it properly.
expected_output: Keeps the project's cn in src/lib/utils.ts and its callers; changes only how it builds twMerge: extendTailwindMerge(withFluid) with withFluid imported from the generated styles/fluid/cn (or as the next argument if it already extends tailwind-merge). Does not create a second cn or copy class groups by hand, and does not edit the generated cn.ts. Runs fluid check, which no longer warns about the cn.
assertions: edits src/lib/utils.ts to use extendTailwindMerge(withFluid)
keeps a single cn: no second cn function, callers unchanged
does not hand-write fluid class groups or edit the generated cn.ts
verifies with fluid check (no tailwind-merge warning)

prompt: On our fluid site the header and nav keep growing on 2560 and 5K screens and look huge. The design says the header should stay at its 1680 size above that, while the page content keeps scaling. How do we do that?
expected_output: Uses a limit in window px, not fixed px on the header's children: sets :root { --fluid-ui-grow-until: 1680; } because the header spends --fluid-ui and --fluid-header-h is built from it, so the header and the page's --fluid-header-h (anchor offsets, hero padding) stay in step; explains that a fluid-grow-until-1680 class on <header> would limit the bar but not --fluid-header-h, and that fluid check warns on it (audit rule header-limit); notes the page content keeps scaling; mentions fluid-grow-until-* on a wrapper for any other component, and fluid explain 2560x1440 to confirm (--fluid-ui 1.167).
assertions: sets --fluid-ui-grow-until: 1680 on :root
explains why not a limit class on <header> (--fluid-header-h would not follow)
does not replace fluid utilities on the header's children with fixed px or max() caps
names the per-component tool for other parts (fluid-grow-until-* on a wrapper)
